governance_justification: Japan's only AI statute, the AI Promotion Act, imposes no enforceable duties or sanctions on private actors, so AI-specific expectations are carried by Cabinet, ministry and J-AISI guidance and a comply-or-explain code, with hard law coming only from general data protection and copyright statutes (a borderline call against Hybrid, because those statutes are not AI-specific).
institutional_map: Japan has no dedicated AI regulator. The Artificial Intelligence Strategic Headquarters (chaired by the Prime Minister and comprising all Cabinet ministers, with the Cabinet Office as secretariat) drafts the AI Basic Plan, adopted the Art. 13 guideline and may request cooperation, but holds no sanctioning power. Operative enforcement sits with existing bodies: the Personal Information Protection Commission over personal data (recommendations and orders backed by criminal penalties now, administrative surcharges once the 2026 amendment commences), and the courts, at the suit of rights holders, under the Copyright Act, on which the Agency for Cultural Affairs offers only interpretive guidance. MIC and METI jointly maintain the voluntary AI Guidelines for Business, J-AISI publishes evaluation guides, and the Cabinet Office IP Strategy Promotion Office receives and lists Principle Code notifications without reviewing them. Overlaps: AI training data engages the PPC and copyright law at once, and the Headquarters guideline overlaps with the MIC/METI guidelines.
conv: Like much of the wider atlas, Japan builds on OECD-style principles (human-centricity, safety, fairness, transparency, accountability) and a proportionate, risk-based approach, and writes the G7 Hiroshima AI Process guiding principles directly into its business guidelines.

Training-data transparency is a shared concern: the EU AI Act requires general-purpose AI model providers to publish a summary of training content (Art. 53(1)(d)), while Japan's Principle Code seeks similar disclosure on a comply-or-explain basis.
gaps: No enforceable AI-specific duties, sanctions or individual remedies bind private developers and deployers, so harms must be pursued through general routes (PPC, copyright, tort). A working group under the Cabinet Office's AI Strategy Expert Panel has tabled a draft outline (18 November 2026) proposing safety and reporting duties, orders and penalties for providers of high-capability AI posing cyber or CBRNE risks, but it is a draft for discussion and nothing has been decided.

Nothing in the register classifies AI systems by risk, prohibits any AI practice, or gives affected persons a right to explanation or human review of automated decisions, leaving high-stakes uses such as hiring, credit and public administration with only voluntary AI-specific safeguards.
assume: Excluded as regulating AI only indirectly: automated-driving road-traffic rules, medical-device approval, financial-sector AI papers, platform and competition laws, and the Digital Agency's guideline on government procurement and use of generative AI; Hiroshima AI Process texts belong on an international plate. Judgement calls: 'AI defined' is Yes only for the AI Promotion Act, whose Art. 2 legally defines 'AI-related technology'; soft-law texts that define terms for their own use are coded No. The Act is coded Binding though its business duties are hortatory; the Basic Plan is Advisory; the J-AISI guide is a Technical standard. Copyright Art. 30-4, the General Understanding, the Act and the Basic Plan carry no pick-list duty. Translation risk: soft-law texts were read in official provisional English translations (the General Understanding in its English overview); J-AISI v1.20 and the 2026 APPI amendment exist only in Japanese and were checked against the official Japanese texts. The team recorded an internal disagreement on whether Art. 30-4 merits its own row or should merge into the General Understanding row; it split them under the codebook's split-when-in-doubt rule, and the editors keep the split. Status verified as of 19-11-2026.

instruments.name: Act on the Protection of Personal Information (APPI)
instruments.original_title: 個人情報の保護に関する法律（平成15年法律第57号）
instruments.systems: Any handling of personal information, including AI training and automated analysis; no AI-specific rules beyond the 2026 consent exemption for statistical uses, which covers AI development
instruments.trigger: Acquiring, using or providing personal information; the 2026 amendment commences in stages: some penalty provisions on 17 January 2027, the rest on a date set by Cabinet Order within two years of promulgation (17 July 2026)
instruments.duties: Transparency; Data governance; Prohibition; Registration or filing
instruments.duty_note: Specify and notify purposes of use, keep data secure and accurate, no improper use or third-party provision without consent (subject to exceptions), report breaches to the PPC
instruments.remedy: PPC recommendations and orders backed by criminal penalties; the 2026 amendment adds administrative surcharges equal to the benefit obtained from serious, large-scale violations (Art. 148-3 et seq., not yet in force)
instruments.gap: Provides no right to explanation or human review of automated decisions and no impact assessment for AI uses, even as the 2026 amendment removes consent for personal data used only for statistical purposes, including AI development.
instruments.citation: Act on the Protection of Personal Information, Act No. 57 of 30 May 2003 (Japan), as amended (official translation current to Act No. 37 of 2021); Act Partially Amending the Act on the Protection of Personal Information and Other Acts, Act No. 56 of 2026, promulgated 17 July 2026 (text published by the PPC: https://www.ppc.go.jp/files/pdf/260717_houritsu.pdf)

instruments.name: Copyright Act, Article 30-4 (Exploitation without the Purpose of Enjoying the Thoughts or Sentiments Expressed in a Work)
instruments.original_title: 著作権法（昭和45年法律第48号）第30条の4
instruments.systems: Use of copyrighted works for data analysis and other non-enjoyment purposes, including AI training; no system categories
instruments.trigger: Exploiting a work where enjoying its expression is not the purpose (e.g. data analysis for AI training); in force 1 January 2019
instruments.duty_note: Imposes no new duty: permits such exploitation unless it would unreasonably prejudice the copyright owner's interests; uses outside the exception fall under ordinary infringement rules
instruments.enf: No regulator named; rights holders enforce in the courts (the Agency for Cultural Affairs issues only interpretive guidance)
instruments.remedy: Injunction, damages and criminal penalties under the Copyright Act where a use falls outside the exception
instruments.gap: Permits training broadly but gives rights holders no notice, opt-out or disclosure mechanism, and its 'unreasonable prejudice' limit is clarified mainly by non-binding agency guidance.
instruments.citation: Copyright Act, Act No. 48 of 6 May 1970 (Japan), Art. 30-4 (inserted by Act No. 30 of 2018); official translation, Japanese Law Translation Database System (Ministry of Justice), current to Act No. 52 of 2021

instruments.name: Act on Promotion of Research and Development, and Utilization of Artificial Intelligence-related Technology (AI Promotion Act)
instruments.original_title: 人工知能関連技術の研究開発及び活用の推進に関する法律（令和7年法律第53号）
instruments.systems: All 'artificial intelligence-related technology', defined functionally in Art. 2; no system categories
instruments.trigger: Developing, providing or using AI in business (Art. 7); in force on promulgation (4 June 2025), with Chapters III-IV (Basic Plan, Strategic Headquarters) from 1 September 2025
instruments.duty_note: No pick-list duty on private actors: businesses must only cooperate with government measures (Art. 7); the State must adopt guidelines (Art. 13), study rights infringements and give guidance (Art. 16), and adopt a Basic Plan (Art. 18)
instruments.enf: None with enforcement power; the AI Strategic Headquarters coordinates and may request cooperation (Arts. 19-20, 25), and the national government may give guidance and advice (Art. 16)
instruments.remedy: None; the Act contains no fines, orders or other sanctions
instruments.gap: Creates no enforceable duties, sanctions or individual remedies for private developers or deployers, whom Art. 7 does not distinguish and asks only to cooperate, so AI harms depend on other laws. Coded Binding as a statute although its business-facing provisions are hortatory; a government working group's draft outline (18 November 2026) proposes legislation imposing safety and reporting duties, orders and penalties on providers of high-capability AI, but nothing has been decided or amended.
instruments.citation: Act on Promotion of Research and Development, and Utilization of Artificial Intelligence-related Technology, Act No. 53 of 4 June 2025 (Japan), Arts. 1-28 and Supplementary Provisions; official translation, Japanese Law Translation Database System (Ministry of Justice)

instruments.name: General Understanding on AI and Copyright in Japan
instruments.original_title: AIと著作権に関する考え方について
instruments.systems: AI training on copyrighted works, generation and use of outputs, and copyrightability of AI-generated material; no system categories
instruments.trigger: Using copyrighted works to develop or train AI, or generating and using outputs similar to existing works
instruments.duty_note: Imposes no duty; sets out the subcommittee's reading of when Art. 30-4 applies and when AI training or outputs may infringe
instruments.enf: None; compiled by the Legal Subcommittee of the Copyright Subdivision, Council for Cultural Affairs; courts decide infringement
instruments.remedy: None of its own; infringement remedies under the Copyright Act apply
instruments.gap: Expressly not legally binding and not a definitive legal assessment, so it gives developers and rights holders no legal certainty and creates no disclosure or opt-out mechanism.
instruments.citation: Legal Subcommittee, Copyright Subdivision, Council for Cultural Affairs, General Understanding on AI and Copyright in Japan (AIと著作権に関する考え方について), 15 March 2024; English overview, Agency for Cultural Affairs, May 2024 (https://www.bunka.go.jp/english/policy/copyright/pdf/94055801_01.pdf)

instruments.name: AI Guidelines for Business (Ver. 1.2)
instruments.original_title: AI事業者ガイドライン（第1.2版）
instruments.systems: AI systems and services across the lifecycle, including advanced AI, AI agents and physical AI; defines 'AI system' for its own purposes while noting AI has no agreed definition
instruments.trigger: Developing, providing or using AI in business activities; voluntary, with no commencement date
instruments.duties: Transparency; Labelling; Risk management; Human oversight; Data governance
instruments.duty_note: Common principles for AI developers, providers and business users, e.g. risk-based governance, information provision, human judgment, and marking AI-generated content
instruments.enf: None; issued jointly by MIC and METI as a living document
instruments.gap: Entirely voluntary with no verification, reporting or enforcement mechanism, and its developer, provider and business-user roles are not tied to legal liability for harm.
instruments.citation: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications and Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, AI Guidelines for Business Ver. 1.2, 31 March 2026; provisional English translation

instruments.name: Guide to Evaluation Perspectives on AI Safety (Version 1.20)
instruments.original_title: AIセーフティに関する評価観点ガイド（第1.20版）
instruments.systems: LLM-based systems and, from v1.20, AI agent systems, with image (multimodal) examples; borrows the AI Guidelines for Business definition of 'AI system'
instruments.trigger: Voluntary safety evaluation by AI developers and providers; v1.20 published 7 July 2026
instruments.duties: Risk management; Audit; Transparency; Data governance
instruments.duty_note: Sets out eleven evaluation perspectives (e.g. harmful output, fairness, privacy, security, explainability, data quality, and observation and control of agents) and example evaluation methods, including red teaming
instruments.enf: None; published by the Japan AI Safety Institute (J-AISI)
instruments.gap: A voluntary method with no pass/fail criteria and no duty to evaluate or disclose results; v1.20 still limits its scope mainly to direct impacts on end users and the external environments a system accesses, leaving socio-technical harms to further study.
instruments.citation: Japan AI Safety Institute, Guide to Evaluation Perspectives on AI Safety (AIセーフティに関する評価観点ガイド), Ver. 1.20, 7 July 2026 (Japanese only; earlier versions 18 September 2024 and 28 March 2025)

instruments.name: Guideline for Ensuring the Appropriateness of Research & Development and Utilization of Artificial Intelligence-Related Technology
instruments.original_title: 人工知能関連技術の研究開発及び活用の適正性確保に関する指針
instruments.systems: All AI-related technology within the AI Promotion Act; risk-based approach without tiers; covers overseas businesses providing AI in Japan
instruments.trigger: Research, development, provision or use of AI; adopted by the AI Strategic Headquarters on 19 December 2025 under Art. 13 of the AI Promotion Act
instruments.duties: Transparency; Labelling; Risk management; Human oversight; Data governance
instruments.duty_note: Asks businesses to build lifecycle AI governance, explain training-data sources and limits, curb harmful outputs, use watermarking or provenance tools as necessary, and asks citizens to keep decisions under human judgment
instruments.enf: None; the guideline is to be reviewed continuously
instruments.gap: Expressly declines to give a single definition or standard of 'appropriateness' and relies on voluntary effort, so no duty can be derived or enforced and affected persons gain no rights.
instruments.citation: Artificial Intelligence Strategic Headquarters, Guideline for Ensuring the Appropriateness of Research & Development and Utilization of Artificial Intelligence-Related Technology, decision of 19 December 2025, under Art. 13 of Act No. 53 of 2025; provisional English translation, Cabinet Office

instruments.name: Artificial Intelligence Basic Plan (Second Plan: “Japan AI Transformation; A Stronger Nation. Greater Prosperity.”)
instruments.systems: Government AI policy on deployment, development, governance and society; no system categories
instruments.trigger: Cabinet decision under Art. 18 of the AI Promotion Act: first plan 23 December 2025, second plan 14 July 2026; the plan itself says it will be revised as needed, in principle annually
instruments.duty_note: Lists government measures, e.g. strengthening J-AISI, issuing guidelines including legal analysis of rights infringement, and continuously reviewing the AI Promotion Act; places no duty on private actors
instruments.enf: None with enforcement power; the AI Strategic Headquarters drafts the plan and promotes and follows up its implementation (Art. 20)
instruments.gap: Defers rather than resolves the core regulatory question: it promises continuous review of the AI Act and legal analysis of rights infringements but sets no timetable, mechanism or sanction for enforceable duties.
instruments.citation: Artificial Intelligence Basic Plan (Second), Cabinet Decision of 14 July 2026, under Art. 18(1) of Act No. 53 of 2025 (first plan: Cabinet Decision of 23 December 2025); provisional English translation, Cabinet Office

instruments.name: Principle Code for the Protection of Intellectual Property and Transparency for the Appropriate Use of Generative AI
instruments.original_title: 生成AIの適切な利活用等に向けた知的財産の保護及び透明性に関するプリンシプル・コード
instruments.systems: Generative AI systems and services provided to the public in Japan, including by overseas businesses; defines 'generative AI' and its developers and providers for its own scope
instruments.trigger: Providing a generative AI system or service to the public in Japan; acceptance notifications to the Cabinet Office opened 26 October 2026
instruments.duties: Transparency; Labelling; Risk management; Data governance; Registration or filing
instruments.duty_note: Comply-or-explain: publish an outline of training data, crawlers, accountability and IP-protection measures (e.g. robots.txt-compliant crawling, watermarking or C2PA), answer narrow training-data disclosure requests (e.g. whether specified URLs were used), and notify acceptance to the Cabinet Office
instruments.enf: Cabinet Office Intellectual Property Strategy Promotion Office receives and lists acceptance notifications without reviewing their content
instruments.remedy: None; comply-or-explain, with reputational consequences only
instruments.gap: Disclosure is comply-or-explain, and rights holders may request only limited information (such as whether specific URLs were used) and only when in or preparing legal proceedings, so they have no enforceable route to learn how their works were used.
instruments.citation: Cabinet Office Intellectual Property Strategy Promotion Office, Principle Code for the Protection of Intellectual Property and Transparency for the Appropriate Use of Generative AI, published 25 August 2026 on the Intellectual Property Strategy Headquarters website after review by the AI-era IP Study Group (13th meeting, 18 August 2026); provisional English translation, Cabinet Office (Japanese text: https://www.cas.go.jp/jp/seisakukaigi/titeki2/ai_kentoukai/kaisai/pdf/ai_principle_code.pdf)
